transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because work has really been getting to me. We got a new operations manager, and she’s been picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years. Since then I can’t seem to leave it at work. I come home all wound up, I snap at my husband, and I lie awake replaying meetings in my head. Then the next day I’m second-guessing routine quality calls I used to make without even thinking.
Have you noticed feeling down, hopeless, or have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or time with family?
I don’t think I’d say hopeless, no. I’m stressed and worn out, but I haven’t really noticed losing interest in my family or things I usually like. It’s more that I’m preoccupied.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, or having trouble controlling your worries, especially about things at work or how you’re doing in your job?

Yes, mostly about work. Since the new operations manager started questioning the inspection procedures I’ve used for years, I keep turning it over in my head. I’ll leave work but still be replaying meetings, wondering if I handled things right, and then the next day I’m second-guessing routine quality calls I used to make without trouble. It’s been hard to shut off.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms, like feeling restless, on edge, or easily fatigued, especially related to this work stress?

Yes, I feel wound up a lot of the time, especially after work. It’s like I can’t leave it there—I come home tense, and then I’m lying awake replaying what was said in meetings. By the next day I’m tired and second-guessing things at work that used to feel routine.
Have you felt down, sad, or have you found less pleasure or enjoyment in things you usually like, even if it’s just for a few days out of the week?
Not really, no. I mean, I have off moments where I feel worn down, but I wouldn’t say I’m feeling sad most of the time or not enjoying things. It’s more like I’m distracted than anything.
Have you found yourself getting more irritable lately, maybe having outbursts or snapping at people more easily than you used to?

Yes, I have. I’ve been snapping at my husband more than I used to, and it’s usually after I come home wound up from work. It’s not like big outbursts, but I’m definitely shorter with him, and I don’t like that.

Have you ever had sudden episodes where you felt intense fear or discomfort that came out of nowhere, like your heart was racing, you couldn’t breathe, or you felt like something terrible was going to happen?
No, I don’t think so. I get tense and stressed, but I haven’t had anything where it suddenly feels like I can’t breathe or something terrible is happening out of nowhere.
Have you, even briefly, felt down or noticed that you’re not enjoying things as much as you usually do, even if it’s just for a short period each day?
Not really. I mean, I might have a few moments where I feel kind of worn out or not fully myself, but I haven’t really noticed feeling down or losing interest in things, even for part of the day.
Outside of work stress, do you find it hard to control worry in other parts of your life, like personal relationships or everyday situations?

It’s mostly tied to work, honestly. Since the new operations manager started questioning the inspection procedures I’ve used for years, I can’t seem to leave it there. I come home still wound up, and then I’ll replay meetings in my head or second-guess decisions I used to make without thinking. It spills over at home, but I wouldn’t say I’m worrying like that about everything in my life.
Outside of the work-related stress, do you find it difficult to control worry or feel physically restless at other times during the day or in other situations?

Not really outside of work. I don’t think I feel restless just out of nowhere during the day. It’s more that if something reminds me of the work situation, then I get wound up again. Otherwise I haven’t noticed it happening in other situations.
Have you been feeling fatigued or low on energy most days, even when you haven’t been doing anything physically or mentally demanding?

I’m not sure I’d say most days. I do get tired sometimes, but I usually feel like it’s tied to being stressed or after a long day. I haven’t really noticed being low on energy when nothing’s been going on.
Outside of your work stress, do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about other things in your life, even just mildly, like responsibilities at home, health, or other everyday matters?

Not really other things, no. It’s mostly this work situation. Since the new operations manager started picking apart the way I’ve done inspections for years, I just can’t leave it there. I come home wound up, and I’ll snap at my husband or lie there replaying meetings. Then at work the next day I start second-guessing routine quality calls I used to make just fine before.
Even after resolving specific stressful work situations in the past, have you found yourself continuing to feel anxious or on edge in general, not tied to any specific problem at work or home?

Not really. This situation hasn’t actually been resolved yet, so I don’t know that I’ve had a chance to see that. I still have to report to him and deal with the procedure changes he made. I haven’t had a stretch afterward where everything was settled but I was still anxious for months on my own.
Even when you’re not thinking about work, do you ever find yourself feeling anxious or on edge without a clear reason?
I don’t think so. If I feel on edge, there’s usually a reason I can point to, and it’s usually work. I haven’t really noticed it coming out of nowhere.
Do you ever find yourself feeling anxious or worried about many different things in life, even when nothing specific is happening or when things are going fine?
No, I don’t think so. I’m not usually worried about a lot of different things when everything’s going okay. It’s more like I can trace it back to something specific.
Has this work-related anxiety affected your ability to function normally in other areas of your life, like home responsibilities or social activities, even when work wasn’t on your mind?

Yes, it has. My work record has definitely taken a hit—I’ve missed some internal deadlines, and I’ve been pulling back from meetings I’m supposed to be in.

At home, too, it’s showing up. My husband and I have been arguing more, and I’m not keeping up with our usual evening routines like I used to. Even if I’m not actively thinking about work, it kind of spills over.
Have there been times when you weren't thinking about work at all where you still felt anxious, worried, or on edge most of the time?

No, not most of the time. If I’m anxious or on edge, it usually ties back to work somehow, even if it’s just in the background. I haven’t noticed feeling that way for no reason when work isn’t on my mind.

F42.9 (Obsessive-compulsive disorder, unspecified) remains due to the intrusive thoughts and second-guessing, though without clear compulsions. F40.11 (Social phobia, generalized type) is retained due to possible social evaluation concerns, though less central. Other disorders like F32.9 (depression), F20.0 (schizophrenia), and dissociative or somatic symptom disorders (F44.1, F44.7) are less consistent with the presentation and are ruled out.

The patient continues to endorse symptoms of anxiety and stress predominantly related to work concerns, without significant features of depression or loss of interest, which makes F43.22 (Adjustment Disorder with Anxiety) and F42.9 (Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder, unspecified) the most plausible. No new information was provided to rule out either condition definitively.
